issues.legal_issue: A seller who has neither obstructed a compulsory purchase nor completion of the sale, but cannot obtain the purchase price because of the purchase order and a court stay, may be awarded interest on the delayed consideration when equity so requires.
material_facts: The seller had agreed to sell the property and had not objected to its compulsory purchase or to completion of the sale to the buyer.
The competent authority made an order to purchase the property, and a court's interim order prevented the matter from being resolved.
The seller could obtain neither the purchase price from the buyer nor payment from the Government while the orders remained in effect.
The Court took account of the increase in the property's market value and the seller's need for money.
issues.conclusion: The interim order was modified to provide for interest from the date of that order: if the compulsory purchase order is upheld, the Government must pay the agreed consideration with interest at 15% per annum; if that order is set aside and the sale to the buyer is completed, the buyer must pay interest at 20% per annum on the unpaid balance. Whether interest is payable, and at what rate, depends on the circumstances of each case.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 269UD of the Income-tax Act, 1961, a compulsory purchase order may prevent completion of an agreement to sell. Where the seller has raised no objection or obstruction to the compulsory purchase or the sale, but cannot obtain the purchase price because of the purchase order and court orders staying the matter, equity may warrant interest at an appropriate rate. The question of entitlement and rate must be determined on the facts and circumstances of each case. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: appeal_from_interim_order and seller_did_not_obstruct_purchase_or_sale and consideration_unavailable_due_to_purchase_order_and_court_stay and equitable_circumstances_support_interest

predicates.appeal_from_interim_order: The proceeding is an appeal concerning an interim order that affects payment or completion of a sale.
predicates.seller_did_not_obstruct_purchase_or_sale: The seller did not object to or obstruct either the compulsory purchase or completion of the agreed sale.
predicates.consideration_unavailable_due_to_purchas: The seller could not obtain the consideration because a compulsory purchase order and a court stay prevented payment or completion.
predicates.equitable_circumstances_support_interest: The circumstances, including the effect of delayed payment on the seller, make an award of interest equitable.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns an interim order and a non-obstructing seller cannot obtain consideration because of a compulsory purchase order and court stay, interest may be awarded if the circumstances make that equitable.
